prompt:
Illustration for a collectible Digimon trading card showing Agumon.
The attached image is a reference sheet of the 3D game model from three sides (3/4, front, side). They are low-polygon PlayStation models: keep each design EXACTLY (proportions, head shape, eyes, claws, colours and markings). KEEP the low-poly look: the visible flat polygon facets and angular, chunky shapes of the model, as in a late-1990s PlayStation 3D game, lit with simple flat shading and a few clean highlights. Make it look like a crisp render from the game's own engine, NOT a glossy modern illustration. Keep the background in the same era: simple, slightly stylised, hand-painted texture-map look, with blocky rocks and plain colour areas, no bokeh, no lens effects, no floating glowing particles, no shiny wet surfaces, no cinematic depth of field.
Pose: lively three-quarter view, full body visible from head to feet. Setting: a blazing volcanic landscape, embers and warm orange-red light, painterly and colourful, with depth behind the creature and a clear single subject.
Composition: the creature centred, filling about 70% of the height, with comfortable margins on every side (the card crops the edges). Soft, even light. No light beams, no god rays, no haze, no glare.
Strictly: no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no border, no card frame, no UI. Square image.
reference: 3D model reference sheet of each species (cardmaker.py ref)
